summary: Implement the frozen event-platform capability with a broker-neutral EventBus contract, strict canonical envelope validation, deterministic Kafka topic/partition mapping, safe producer requirements, and bounded at-least-once retry/dead-letter semantics without introducing Kafka imports into domain code.

impacts.evidence: The canonical envelope requires organization/workspace identifiers and the Kafka partition key binds both tenant identifiers with entity type/id so identical external aggregate identifiers in different tenants do not share ordering identity.

Event payloads are preserved rather than silently redacted because legitimate business data can be classified personal; retry/DLQ metadata contains only bounded machine codes and documentation explicitly applies source-topic privacy/retention rules to dead letters.
No REST/OpenAPI surface is changed by this task; EventBus is an internal platform port consumed later by application/domain workflows.

The existing published event-envelope ID/pattern is preserved while runtime validation, EventType version parsing, deterministic family topic routing and a new delivery-metadata contract establish the transport compatibility boundary.
Future connector/plugin code will depend on approved platform event abstractions rather than Kafka internals; this task does not alter Connector SDK admission or add a provider branch.
Task 007 adds no database schema. Transactional event persistence is intentionally deferred to Task 008 Outbox so this task cannot create a false DB-to-Kafka atomicity claim.

Envelope decoding rejects duplicate/unknown fields and bounded payload violations; Kafka system headers are unique and verified against the envelope; raw handler/client error text is not propagated into transport headers or adapter errors.
Event transport does not authorize sensitive business actions; Task 017 remains the approval/risk gate and EventBus only transports already-authorized domain facts.

Immutable event ID, correlation/causation, actor/trace, source, tenant and aggregate metadata provide deterministic lineage fields and retry preserves the original immutable event body and identifier.

Delivery is explicitly at-least-once; publish-before-commit retry/DLQ routing can duplicate replacement records after crashes, and Task 009 is explicitly retained as the mandatory consumer deduplication boundary.
No webhook delivery/signing surface changes; later webhook workers may consume EventBus but remain independently durable and signed under Task 063.
The Kafka design now defines producer error/latency, consumer lag, retry/DLQ rate and age, partition/ISR/auth/quota signals as required production observability inputs for later SLO/runbook tasks.

There is no persistence migration, but deployment must preserve topic/version compatibility and retry/DLQ retention; rollback remains source/config rollback while Kafka replay continues from committed offsets.

Unit tests cover strict event JSON, topic/partition mapping, unsafe producer rejection, handler success, retry/backoff, permanent and exhausted failures, invalid/tampered records, cancellation, and the invariant that source commit occurs only after replacement publication.
